subject: Middle School Grade Configuration Task Force Report
overview: The Committee reviewed significant reports on English learner proficiency and the Grade Configuration Task Force, which concluded that a proposed middle school grade split is not feasible due to facility constraints. The body also discussed the 2027-2028 school calendar and a potential delayed opening policy.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved the consent agenda, including bills, payrolls, budget transfers, and meeting minutes from October and November.

items.title: Mustang Moment: McGlynn Middle School
items.summary: Received a presentation highlighting student belonging at McGlynn Middle School through athletic championships and the Tufts University Hillel Community Action Partners mentorship program.

items.title: ACCESS Testing and English Learner Update
items.summary: Reviewed data on English language proficiency and the academic performance of former English learners, noting substantial growth at the elementary level but declining progress at the secondary level.

items.title: 2027-2028 District Calendar
items.summary: Tabled the 2027-2028 school calendar to allow for further review of professional development days and religious holiday observations with the Professional Development Advisory Committee.

items.title: Grade Configuration Task Force Findings
items.summary: Approved task force recommendations to investigate a single comprehensive middle school model and form an advisory committee on educational frameworks after finding that a proposed 5-6 and 7-8 grade split is not viable due to facility constraints at Andrews Middle School.

items.title: Policy JG-R: Elementary School Reassignment
items.summary: Tabled the second reading of the elementary school reassignment policy to refine language regarding sibling placement and family logistics.

items.title: Feasibility of Delayed School Openings
items.summary: Approved a request for a feasibility study on implementing delayed openings for inclement weather or operational challenges, with a report due in January.
